<reason>Side A won by demonstrating that expanded authentication and risk absorption are economically unworkable for low-value resale due to flat logistics costs versus percentage commissions, and by exposing that Side B's proposed alternatives (AI screening, photo forensics) contradict their opening claims or fail to prevent buyer swap-fraud without physical custody. Side A successfully forced Side B to concede that physical verification is necessary (B5.4), which then made the cost argument decisive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Rebuttal 2, which exposed Side B's retreat from custody chains to "photo forensics" (contradicting B's opening claim that photos cannot verify authenticity) and turned B's "tier fees" suggestion into evidence that the motion would raise costs for ordinary consumers.</best_rebuttal>
